info.name: Token Payments Local Cookie Auth
info.description: Local Token Payments auth requests for validating HttpOnly cookie session transport and signed CSRF double-submit flow. Postman stores Set-Cookie responses in its cookie jar; happy-path requests after login intentionally omit manual Cookie headers so the jar sends access_token, refresh_token, and csrf_token.

item.name: Cookie Auth Happy Path
item.description: Run these requests in order. The challenge and login responses set cookies; Postman keeps them in the cookie jar and later sends them without a manual Cookie header.

item.name: 1. Request login challenge
item.description: Issues the SIWE v1 MetaMask signing message and signed CSRF token. Postman stores the csrf_token Set-Cookie value in the cookie jar. EOA and deployed ERC-1271 smart wallet signatures use the same SIWE message contract.

exec: pm.test("challenge response exposes signing message and CSRF", function () {
pm.expect(body.signingMessage).to.include("wants you to sign in with your Ethereum account:");
pm.test("Postman cookie jar contains CSRF cookie", function () {

header.value: csrf_token=<redacted-signed-csrf-token>; Max-Age=3600; Expires=<bounded-http-date>; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax

item.name: 2. Login with MetaMask signature
item.description: Paste a local MetaMask personal_sign result into the environment before running. EOA accounts and deployed ERC-1271 smart wallets are supported; linked wallets and ERC-6492 are future scope. The response stores access_token and refresh_token in the Postman cookie jar and returns only <set-cookie> markers in the body.

item.description: Verifies a WALLET_LINK SIWE message and links the wallet to the authenticated user.

item.description: Lists wallets linked to the authenticated user.

item.name: Set primary wallet
item.description: Marks one verified active wallet as primary for its chain.

item.name: Revoke wallet
item.description: Revokes a linked wallet while keeping at least one verified active wallet.

item.name: 3. Refresh session with cookie jar
item.description: Postman sends the refresh_token from the cookie jar. Do not add a manual Cookie header; only echo the latest csrfToken in X-CSRF-Token.

item.name: 4. Logout with cookie jar
item.description: Postman sends the current auth cookies from the cookie jar. Logout is mutating, so X-CSRF-Token must use the latest csrfToken variable.

exec: if (!pm.environment.get("csrfToken")) { throw new Error("csrfToken is required for cookie-authenticated logout."); }

item.description: Safe GET request. When run before logout, Postman sends access_token from the cookie jar; X-CSRF-Token is not required for safe methods.
